fields.why: No difference or ratio is reported: group contrasts are wording backed by 't-tests with p<0.05', and the only percentage-point figure ('approximately 2.5 percentage points lower') is cited from an earlier report, as A's own notes say. B's null matches the side-by-side rule and the equity cap both readers applied; A's 'absolute' is defensible because t-tests of differences in proportions are on the absolute scale.

Sex appears only in the weighting note ('population control totals for age group, sex, metropolitan statistical area status, education...'); the brief records sex always, here as a covariate/weighting role without raising the level. A missed it.

brief_issues: The brief should say whether a test of a difference whose size is never reported (t-tests behind 'higher than' wording) sets comparison.scale to absolute or leaves it null; the equity level-2 cap ('significance marks only') implies null.
